name: Amirudin Shari
_note: M2 state-executive cohort (Phase 2). Menteri Besar of Selangor since 2018 (second term from 21 Aug 2023). Added as a PH-aligned rich-state executive to balance the sub-national-executive class across coalitions and capacity. Provisional Layer B anchors pending the blind panel (minCodersToScore=3). Citations search-corroborated; reconfirm against primary sources. A5 none-on-record: third parties have lodged complaints (LLSB defamation, since resolved in his administration's favour; the MBI sand-mining probe named no charge against him) but he is not charged. 3R: B5 left unscored (the Dengkil temple/mosque-land dispute is a contested flashpoint).

metrics.justification: No charge or conviction against Amirudin personally; the one related matter to reach court, a defamation suit over a state river project, ended with the accuser apologising and admitting the claims were baseless (Feb 2025), and an MACC probe of state vehicle MBI (which he chairs ex officio) named no charge against him. Recorded as the subject's own status: none on record.

metrics.justification: In the December 2021 floods, Selangor was the hardest-hit state (17 deaths and tens of thousands displaced, with Taman Sri Muda residents stranded for days); he requested federal and military assets and attributed delays to the federal disaster chain of command, and the response was widely criticised as slow. Adequate response with mixed, criticised outcomes (anchor 2).

citation.title: Malaysia warns of more floods as Prime Minister admits lapse in rescue efforts

metrics.justification: The Skim Air Darul Ehsan free-water scheme (20 cubic metres a month) reached about 340,000 accounts by October 2024, which he candidly noted was below the 600,000-account target; the scheme and the Iltizam Selangor Sihat health subsidy were inherited from his predecessor and scaled rather than originated. Partial delivery against target, sustained not originated (anchor 2).

After the August 2023 state election he formed a 10-member executive council that for the first time in 15 years included Barisan Nasional (one UMNO seat alongside nine Pakatan Harapan), and has since defended that cross-coalition arrangement against calls to drop the UMNO member. Documented cross-coalition governing consensus (anchor 3).
